newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks leave Deng fears behind, end buoyant.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks leave Deng fears behind, end buoyant.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks blazed ahead on Thursday to close with buoyant gains after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping allowed investors to put recent uncertainty behind them.
The Hang Seng Index soared 305.01 points, or 2.33 percent, to close at 13,411.33. The index shrugged off an opening loss of 92 points and climbed to a high of 13,427.02 during the session.
"I think what you see today is a really typical 'sell the rumour, buy the news'," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston.
Turnover improved compared with recent sessions, rising to a hefty HK$11.37 billion versus HK$7.12 billion on Wednesday.
China announced Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
"This is something that stock markets have been gearing up for for some considerable time," said Peter Churchouse, regional strategist at Morgan Stanley.

"People have got used to the idea and thought long and hard about likely directions in China post-Deng anyway. People have got their own views and have become more or less comfortable with them," he said.

Concerns about Deng Xiaoping's health contributed to a recent slide in Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index. From an all-time high of 14,004.93 on January 16, the blue chip barometer had tumbled 899 points to Wednesday's close of 13,106.32.
"It was seen as getting back into buy territory again," said Pauline Gately, regional strategist at Merrill Lynch.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said investors felt that "the last detectable uncertainty in China has been removed with the death of Deng Xiaoping".
"Based on the fundamentals and the economic development in China, there should be further upside potential," he said.
Many analysts said they were not expecting significant policy changes in China following Deng's death.
"China has made huge progress during the years of Deng Xiaoping and I guess that people are expecting that should continue," said Verin.
February Hang Seng futures also surged, climbing 405 points to close at 13,485.
Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International, said investors were looking forward to a new phase of the market.
"They are probably looking at the 14,000 level with this kind of buying momentum," he said.
